t: #3376 Minimum Time to Break Locks I
o: The sword's energy grows by factor x each minute, where x starts at 1 and increases by k after each lock broken — so x depends only on HOW MANY locks are broken so far, not which. Breaking lock i as the (m+1)-th lock takes ceil(strength[i]/x) minutes with x = 1 + m·k. With n ≤ 8, try all 2^n subsets: dp[mask] = minimum minutes to break the locks in mask; extending by any unbroken lock adds ceil(strength[i]/(1+popcount·k)).
k: The sword factor depends only on popcount(mask), so subset DP over masks is valid despite ordering effects.
Cost of breaking lock i next is ceil(strength[i]/(1 + k·popcount(mask))) — an independent additive term.
n ≤ 8 gives 256 masks × 8 transitions — trivially fast.

a.i: Process masks in increasing order; from each mask, try breaking any remaining lock next, paying ceil(strength/x) with x determined by popcount. The optimal order emerges from the DP without enumerating permutations explicitly.
s: For each reachable mask, set x = 1 + k·popcount(mask).
For each unbroken i, relax dp[mask | 1<<i] with dp[mask] + ceil(strength[i]/x).
a.sp: O(2^n) — the DP array over masks.

a.i: Equivalent top-down formulation: dfs(mask) returns the minimum additional time to finish from state mask; trying every remaining lock as the next target generates all orderings with shared subproblems memoized.
s: dfs(mask): if mask is full return 0.
For each unbroken i, candidate = ceil(strength[i]/x) + dfs(mask | 1<<i).
Return the minimum candidate; memoize on mask.
a.t: O(2^n · n) — same state space as bottom-up, visited lazily.
a.sp: O(2^n) — memoization array plus recursion stack O(n).

w: Bitmask DP is the canonical answer; the greedy 'always break the cheapest next lock' fails because a stronger sword later can make an expensive lock cheap. Ceiling division and the popcount-dependent factor are the two details to get right. Edge cases: n = 1, huge strength values (use 64-bit intermediates). Follow-up: version II with larger n (Hungarian-style or different structure), or return the optimal breaking order.
